long_biography.plain_text:
Johan Hartman grew up in a Dutch family of skipper-owners whose maritime lineage reaches back centuries. In 2003 he established Hartman Marine Group in Urk, combining commercial shipbuilding, pleasure-craft construction and oceangoing transport. Its early cargo designs sought more speed and lifting capacity without the operating costs of much larger vessels. A fast multipurpose ship from the yard won the Dutch Ship of the Year award, and the group later developed compact heavy-lift vessels for wind-energy components.

Hartman extended that engineering approach into a pleasure-craft division. He built an explorer cruiser initially for family voyaging, with a classic profile and practical ocean-going construction. Shipbuilding remains central to the enterprise: the Urk yard has continued developing efficient vessels, including a sustainable mini heavy-lifter for offshore wind work. His family background gave him deep maritime experience, while the yard and its vessel designs were built under his own direction.
